events.title: McCabe & Mrs. Miller (1971) *CUG Film Society Film Meetup*

If your domain isn’t set up to block fakes, anyone can put your exact email address on a fake message, and many inboxes will deliver it. AI tools make fake emails and invoices look more convincing, so an email that looks right is no longer proof that it’s real.
In October 2026, Raileon checked the public email settings of 749 South Florida law firms and real estate offices. About 4 in 5 haven’t told inboxes to block fake email in their name.

events.description:
The ecological intimacy of a swamp, none of the physical inconveniences. In the Lab: The Little Wetland brings children face-to-face with living swamp flora, including aquatic carnivorous plants. Children study the plants in individual aquariums, then come together to create a miniature living wetland in a shallow vessel.

About Sasha Sikaffy:
Sasha S. Sikaffy, M.S., is an environmental scientist and educator informed by years spent in coral reef fieldwork and marine science education.

events.description: Uncover the history of one of New York City’s oldest and most culturally diverse neighborhoods! This class emphasizes subtle body awareness and nervous system support, with helpful verbal cues and gentle assists offered throughout the practice. Each session closes with a longer savasana to rest deeply and absorb the nurturing energy of the garden, supporting integration.
“It’s not a performance, it’s an inward journey.”

events.title: From Plant to Music
events.description:
Join Miami-based musician and artist Bruno Esposito for a hands-on exploration of how plant materials become music. Discover the guacharaca, its Indigenous roots and role in Colombian Caribbean traditions, and the natural materials behind gaitas, maracas, and drums. Explore how plants, craftsmanship, rhythm, and culture come together to create sound.

This special Subtropicalist gathering is free and open to all Garden Circle Members to attend!

Join Columbia Business School's Doron Nissim, Ernst & Young Professor…

events.description: "It's okay with me" is the signature, rumpled life motto of private investigator Philip Marlowe, played by Elliott Gould, in Robert Altman's 1973 revisionist film noir adaptation of The Long Goodbye by Raymond Chandler. Marlowe mumbles this at everyone and everything, including the murder he was framed for in Altman's depiction of 1970s Los Angeles.

events.description: A young girl wanders through the cathedral-like ruins of a strange city, caring for a large egg as she's trailed by a wandering soldier who's waiting to see what's inside of it. Mamoru Oshii directs the story with little dialogue or explanation; instead he builds from Yoshitaka Amano's gothic, waterlogged production design and biblical deluge.

events.description:
Join the CBS Cocktails & Spirits Club for an evening at New York Distilling Company in Bushwick with co-founder Tom Potter ‘83.

Tom started out as a banker before co-founding Brooklyn Brewery in 1987 and turning it into one of the country’s best-known craft beer brands. In 2011 he did it again with New York Distilling Company, bringing back the city’s pre-Prohibition distilling tradition with whiskey and gin made from New York–grown grain.
